chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who intends to perform Hajj: should he trim his hair during the months of Hajj? He said: 'No, and not from his beard, but he should trim his mustache and his nails, and let him trim [his hair] if he wishes.'
As for what indicates that if he shaves his head in Dhi al-Qa'dah, a sheep's blood [sacrifice] is due upon him, then what he narrated:

key_terms.أَشْهُرُ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and part of Muharram)
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhu al-Qa'dah (one of the months of Hajj)
key_terms.لْيَطَّلِ: Let him trim (imperative form indicating permission)
key_terms.يَأْخُذُ: To take/trim (implies partial removal, not complete shaving)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for trimming hair and nails during Hajj for a Muhrim?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific grooming permissions for a Muhrim during the months of Dhu al-Qadah and Dhu al-Hijjah, distinguishing between permissible trimming of the mustache and nails and the prohibition of shaving the head. It highlights the scholarly distinction between 'taking from' hair (trimming) and 'removing' it (shaving), noting that while shaving is not strictly forbidden, it incurs a sacrificial penalty (dam) if performed before the completion of Hajj rites. This ruling underscores the balance between maintaining personal hygiene and preserving the sanctity of the Ihram state in Shia jurisprudence.
